column2: I shouted, fed up and desperate!
We climbed to the summit together and decided to take on an advanced course called the Ultra Expert Special Thunder Dragon Raaah!{p}Taaah!{p}Hyaaah!{p}Course
, which had an absurdly long name.
The slope looked cut straight up and down, covered in moguls and, on top of that, rock-hard ice.
Because of the blizzard, visibility was only a few yards.
In the sky, as the course name said, thunder like dragons, that is, dragon-shaped lightning, streaked across.
Skiers charred black by lightning strikes lay groaning here and there.
I flashed her a grin and launched myself down the slope.
Using the spring in my legs and hips to dodge the moguls, I shot down like an arrow.
I jumped off an especially big mogul!
And spun three times in midair.
The astonished and admiring looks of the skiers around me...
That's right, I was actually a genius skier, and I was competing in the Olympics right now.
Red and blue gates raced toward me.
Knocking those gates aside, I cut through the wind.
Just a little more, just a little more to the finish.
Soon the gold medal would be in my hands...
I could hear {n2} cheering me on.
Ah, my face is freezing cold.
The finish is so close, and yet it's so cold, so cold I could die...
A slap hit my face and my vision blurred.
Someone's face floated up in my blurry vision.
Straining to focus, it turned into {n2}'s face.
I seemed to be lying on my back.
I asked {n2} as I sat up.
“Don't you remember?{r}{p}You went off the course, slid and slid down, and hit this tree.{r}{p}...Are you hurt anywhere?”
Sure enough, a big white birch stood in front of me.
My body was buried in fresh powder, and my skis and poles stuck out in random directions a little way off.
Since it didn't hurt when I struggled, it seemed I hadn't broken a leg or anything.
With {n2}'s help, I finally managed to crawl out of the powder.
“It looks like you hit your head, so I'll drive.”
By the time we reached the parking lot it was completely dark, and on top of that it had started snowing.
If you do that, we'll get lost in the snow!”
Don't be so dramatic.{r}{p}That can't happen.”
True enough.{r}{p}I just had a bad feeling.”
By the time we reached the parking lot it was completely dark, and on top of that it had started snowing.
We fixed the skis to the roof of the 4WD, I got in the passenger seat, and {n2} got in the driver's seat.
I could tell she was nervous, and that made me a little uneasy.
you do have a license, right?”
Before I could even buckle my seat belt, the car shot off.
When I yelled in terror, {n2} answered with a serious look.
I made her stop the car.
The blizzard was getting worse, and this was suicidal.
Let's leave the car and catch a taxi.{r}{p}That's the only way.”
Luckily we caught a taxi right away, and we reached the inn 'Spur' safely.
if she can drive like that, no license needed, I figured.
I screamed and braced both legs against the floor.
{n2} drove clinging to the wheel, glaring at the outside.
{n2} slammed the brakes and turned the wheel, and the car left the road and plowed into a drift with a thud
The seat belt dug into my shoulder and for a moment I couldn't breathe.
Neither of us could speak for a while.
Could I have seen it wrong?
Maybe I mistook a giant praying mantis...
{n2} shook her head to deny it.
I heard about it as a kid.{r}{p}My grandfather ran into one, they say.{r}{p}He showed me the scar from then.{r}{p}It was about two inches long.”
...More to the point, get the car moving already.”
Was he pulling my leg after all...”
{n2} murmured, tilting her head, somehow got the car back on the road, and started driving carefully.
I met {n2} this summer on the roof of a department store.
It was a part-time job at an event.
She played the heroine of a Super Sentai-style show, and I was the sea cucumber monster she defeated.
Since we'd arrived at the inn, I banished the humiliating memory from my head and got out of the car.
This inn is run by {n2}'s uncle and his wife.
“No, it's just that the inn's name seems to have changed...”
“The name can't change while we're out skiing, can it?{r}{p}Did you hit your head or something?”
It's similar, but it feels a little different somehow...”
Stepping inside, Mr. Kobayashi's voice greeted us warmly.
But somehow his face seemed a little different.
Looking again, even the inside of the inn looked different from when we left.
But when I went up to the second floor, to my astonishment even the positions of the rooms were different.
“This is that legendary place where the map changes every time you enter...”
{n2} and I turned and stared at the door to the basement.
They say that deep underground there's a rare treasure no one has ever brought back...
We went up to our rooms for a moment to change,
and met in the common room by the entrance on the first floor.
what's the name of this inn again?”
'Spur,' of course.{r}{p}Did you forget even that?”
“The 'Box of Cold Sweat,' full of suspense.”
We went back to our rooms for a moment to change,
and met in the common room by the first-floor entrance.
Some people were relaxing on the sofas around the big table until dinner started.
Looks like you got in plenty of skiing.”
The one who greeted me so breezily when he saw me was a man named Mr. Kayama.
Apparently in his youth he was called the “Young Boss of the Alps” and was good at both sports and singing
“Oh, you're not that Mr. Kayama, you're this Mr. Kayama.
Yes, Mr. Kayama was the president of a company in Osaka, and anything but a breath of fresh air.
Oops, I'd said it out loud.{g}
Mr. Kayama's wife was far too beautiful for him.
How did she marry such a dull man?
That wife smiled seductively and spoke to me.
Ditch that old baldy and elope with me!”
Pale blue flames were blazing behind {n2}!
“I was obviously joking.{r}{p}I'm devoted to {n2} alone.”
it was a joke?{r}{p}What a shame.”
The wife said it with a sad face.
But remembering there were other women too, I pulled myself together.
Of course, I meant the three office ladies who had apparently arrived today.
One was the slender, long-haired Kanako Watase.
She was quite a beauty too.
I felt like I'd had a close encounter with her somewhere before.
The plump one was Keiko Kitano.
The other was Aki Kawamura, who looked great in glasses.
The pattern of being a beauty once the glasses come off is hard to pass up, too.
“What do you mean, hard to pass up?”
I'd said what I was thinking out loud again.
There was also a woman named Midori working part-time, but I decided to pass on her.
Somehow I had a feeling she was already seeing the guy who works there part-time.
And younger is better, after all.
“Don't get that drooling look on your face!”
{n2}'s Special Paper Fan Chop went off.
The sound of a car engine approached.
The engine went around from the back to the front...
With the scream came a huge crash.
A man covered in blood came in.
“Anyway, first sign the register at the front desk...”
As he signed, the man called Mikimoto groaned.
“How fortunate, you made it in time for dinner...”
With the sound of the cuckoo clock, Midori came out of the dining room.
She didn't change expression at the sight of the blood-covered guest either.
Everyone here seemed incapable of reacting to sudden changes.
We went into the dining room and sat at a table.
Right away my eyes landed on a man in the corner with a bizarre aura.
He wore a micro-mini red dress with cute frills, with purple eye shadow and lipstick.
On his head was a giant polka-dot ribbon.
“He should pick clothes that fit his age.”
“His clothes and makeup don't go together.”
{n2} held her head and slumped onto the table.
Then she hurriedly lowered her voice and went on.
Maybe he heard my voice: a low, hoarse voice rang out from the corner.
It's rude to call a cross-dresser gay.{r}{p}Apologize to the cross-dresser.”
Now {n2} would stop judging people by their appearance so carelessly.
As I savored {n2}'s growth in my heart, the food arrived.
The first soup was something called Fo-Chew or F-You, a Chinese soup.
I think it was so delicious that a monk went to the neighbor's house to borrow rice, and that's how it got its name, or something...
“That's not it at all!{r}{p}The monk jumped over the wall!”
“Do you eat this with the fish knife?”
{n2} asked me, and I started thinking.
no, an amphibian.{r}{p}If it's an amphibian, the fish knife should do, right?”
Right, it'd be different if it were a reptile, but it's an amphibian.{r}{p}Practically a fish.”
With that, {n2} ate the newt with relish.
I was glad she'd learned the proper manners.
{n2} exclaimed the moment she took a bite.
It was a taste I'd never experienced.
Rich with fat, yet surprisingly not heavy, with a lingering flavor.
I called over Midori, the part-timer.
When I asked, Midori's face suddenly turned pale.
no, I'm not complaining or anything...{r}{p}It's really delicious, I just don't know what meat it is...”
But Midori looked away and fled to the kitchen.
...that's strange.{r}{p}I only asked what meat it was...”
It was delicious either way, so I decided not to worry about it.
there's a karaoke set over there.”
I was tired and not in the mood at all.
“Don't say that...{p}I wonder what songs they have...”
“Oh, that doesn't work...{r}{p}It's broken, and only one song plays now.”
Mr. Kobayashi answered from the kitchen.
what a letdown.{r}{p}Oh well, let's try it.”
{n2} set up the song and came back with the microphone.
At night, the basement is scary
and you lock me in by force, you good-for-nothing
A man's life that bloomed in Osaka
Never thought it would scatter in Nagano
Next time I die, next time I go
I'll die peacefully on a tatami mat
Everyone else was gathered in the common room.
I was determined to find out what this meat was, no matter what.
I stood up and tiptoed after Midori.
Just then, from somewhere far off, I heard a voice like a scream.
...{n2}, didn't you just hear a scream?”
It definitely sounded like a scream.”
A terrible thought suddenly came to me.
A scream from somewhere in the building...
Putting these together, only one thing came to mind.
The voice seemed to come from deep inside the building.
I went down the first-floor hallway.
It was definitely a woman's scream.
But the end of the hallway was a storeroom.
Inside the storeroom there was another door.
Beyond it was a staircase leading down.
I swallowed hard and started down the stairs one step at a time.
It was clearly coming from the bottom of the stairs.
I carefully descended the last few steps without letting them creak.
Cardboard boxes and wooden crates were piled up messily in the dim light.
It seemed to be a storage room for food and such.
A voice came from beyond the stacked boxes.
now how shall I prepare this one...”
It was Mr. Kobayashi's voice, but in a more sinister tone than I'd ever heard.
Wanting to see what was going on, I quietly peeked out from behind the boxes.
Mr. Kobayashi stood there with a devilish grin, gripping a kitchen knife.
Mr. Kobayashi casually grabbed it and chopped its head off with the knife!
Would you stop screaming every time?
So he'd just been killing a chicken...
We climbed the stairs and returned to the dining room.
After finishing our after-dinner coffee, everyone gathered in the common room.
I asked, and Mr. Kobayashi answered.
“He said he wanted to fix his makeup and went back to his room.”
With that heavy makeup, fixing it must be a big job.
Just then, all the lights suddenly went out.
The girls' screams flew around in the darkness.
I sensed Kyoko stand up in the dark and go off somewhere.
About five minutes later, Kyoko came back carrying a lit candle.
To my astonishment, Kyoko was wearing lace-up boots and a black leather bondage outfit.
And along with the candle, she even had a leather whip...
Kyoko set the candle on the table and disappeared into the darkness.
The flickering candlelight lit the faces of everyone around the table, making it look like some sinister gathering.
“...This is something that really happened to my friend's younger sister...”
“She was bad at math...{r}{p}and had to take summer remedial classes...”
Before I knew it, Kyoko had changed and come back too.
“People left as they finished their assignments, and she was apparently the last one left.{r}{p}...And then something terrible happened.”
“After she finally finished the assignment, she went to the bathroom.{r}{p}She'd been holding it the whole time and there was no way she could last until she got home.{r}{p}But then...”
“...And she failed math in the end, and ever since then that bathroom has been called the 'cursed toilet'...”
Everyone fell silent for a while at the unexpectedly horrifying story.
Then a scream that sounded neither male nor female came from the second floor.
Mr. Kobayashi took the candle and started up the stairs.
Several of us, myself included, followed.
Mr. Kobayashi called in a trembling voice.
Had that scream been from him?
Mr. Kobayashi knocked on Mr. Tanaka's door.
The door seemed unlocked, and Mr. Kobayashi opened it slowly.
Inside the room it was, of course, pitch dark.
When Mr. Kobayashi cautiously held the candlelight inside, we saw the legs of what looked like a fallen person.
Two legs in bright red high heels...
'She' had changed into a blood-red evening dress.
A muscular chest showed through the deep neckline, and even in stockings it was clear that the thick legs were very hairy.
The eyes, painted with eye shadow like a bruise, were wide open in surprise.
{n2} asked in a hushed voice to no one in particular.
Mr. Kobayashi shook his head, approached, and put a hand on Mr. Tanaka's shoulder, shaking it.
Then I noticed 'she' was holding a small board in her left hand.
The board was smeared with blood.
Suddenly, an idea flashed through my mind.
“A cross-dresser ('okama') dead, gripping a bloody board ('ita')...
...No, this was no time to cheer when someone had been killed.
I looked around at everyone's faces and spoke.

“Now, in a case like this, it's an established rule that the culprit is among us.{r}{p}The culprit that Mr. Tanaka pointed out with his dying strength must be in this room.{r}{p}...Everyone, please gather in the common room.”
Gathered in the common room, I studied everyone's faces.
Then I noticed a man tiptoeing toward the front door.
Dressed all in black, wearing a ski mask, with a bloody kitchen knife in his hand.
A man I'd never seen before.
Suddenly under everyone's gaze, the man answered in confusion.
Let me guess...{p}It's obvious from that knife.{r}{p}You're...
a fishmonger just passing through, aren't you?”
“You don't need to say it, I understand!{r}{p}In this blizzard,
delivering fish is tough, so of course you need a ski mask.{r}{p}That explains everything.{r}{p}...So we can rule this man out.{r}{p}A fishmonger just passing by wouldn't
kill a guest of the inn.”
the culprit must be among those who remain.{r}{p}We need to check alibis for the time Mr. Tanaka is thought to have been killed.”
“But when we heard the scream, everyone was here, weren't we?”
I shook my head at {n2}'s words.
the power was out then.{r}{p}Someone could have sneaked upstairs.”
“I was definitely here.{r}{p}I'm the one who went up with the candle, after all.”
Then let's rule out Mr. Kobayashi too.”
“We were all together the whole time too,
“We can't trust only the testimony of friends and spouses.{r}{p}Does anyone know that they were here the whole time?”
Two people timidly raised their hands.
Then we'll accept these three alibis too.”
Continuing to confirm alibis like that, strangely enough, it turned out everyone had one.
This is odd.{r}{p}At this rate, nobody could have killed Mr. Tanaka.”
The man in black, the fishmonger, suddenly grew fidgety.
“It has nothing to do with you, so please be quiet and watch me solve the mystery.”
“Solve the mystery? Do you have some idea, {n1}?”
they used a trick!{r}{p}It must be a trick!”
when the scream was heard, everyone was downstairs...{p}So this...
they killed Mr. Tanaka upstairs while staying on the first floor.”
“For example... secretly tie a string to Mr. Tanaka's foot and pull it all the way here.{r}{p}Then, timed with the blackout, yank it as hard as you can.”
“If the power hadn't gone out, that string would have been visible!”
“Of course, the blackout was the culprit's doing.”
“...Let's change our way of thinking.{r}{p}Listen up.
Mr. Tanaka left a dying message that means 'kamaitachi.'{r}{p}If we think about who that points to, the culprit should be obvious.”
The unrelated fishmonger tried to cut in again, so I glared at him.
“Of course, nobody has a name like that, but something about their appearance or whatever must resemble a 'kamaitachi.'”
“What kind of person resembles a kamaitachi?”
well, someone who looks like a weasel, I'd guess.”
I said and looked around, but nobody looked like a weasel.
Midori and Toshio suddenly spoke at the same time.
Speaking simultaneously, it was like stereo.
“They say the kamaitachi is a yokai {C3}(supernatural creature){C0} made up of three beasts.”
They harmonized perfectly on that last part.
All eyes focused on the three office ladies.
wait a minute!{r}{p}Are you saying the three of us did it?”
“If you're going to say that, I'll say something too.{r}{p}You
look quite a bit like a weasel.”
And you've got a face like a tanuki {C3}(Japanese raccoon dog){C0}!”
Grrr!{r}{p}That's what I'm self-conscious about, you hag!”
The topic seemed to have drifted off course.
“Now, now, you two, what matters now is the murder case.”
This is more important right now!”
...Since they shouted at me at the same time, I decided to ignore the two still glaring at each other.
“Whether they look alike or not is hard to judge, so let's look at it another way.”
Don't you think this name sounds quite a lot like kamaitachi?”
No way, no matter how you look at it.”
For a moment, a silence as if time had stopped ruled the common room.
“Yelling out of nowhere, who exactly are you...”
Can't you tell from how I'm dressed?{r}{p}I'm the one who did it!
I stabbed him to death with this knife!”
Jokes like that won't go over, Mr. Fishmonger.”
This is a knife I took from the kitchen to kill that guy!”
“How could I possibly look like a fishmonger?
Are your eyes rotten?{p}I'm a bartender at a snack bar!”
I asked cautiously, and he lowered his eyes sadly.
She came alone to my bar, and while I was serving her, we... {p}we fell in love.”
Groans of “ugh” rose from all around.
but she never said a word... {p}that she was a man!”
couldn't you tell he was a man just by looking?”
“I never imagined a man could be that beautiful.{r}{p}I know...
Well, there's no accounting for taste...
the truth is, I still love her...
no, the bartender dropped the knife to the floor and began to weep openly.
It was a love story as beautiful as it was sad.{r}{p}It's clear everything went exactly as I deduced.”
“However, there's one thing I don't understand.{r}{p}What on earth that dying message was pointing to.”
I'm Kamai Tatsuro, so everybody calls me Kamaitachi.”
...not thinking it was a name was my blind spot.”
Outside, the blizzard kept raging as ever.
Kamai collapsed on the floor and kept crying, stifling his voice.
“This case was the hardest and the saddest of any I've solved so far.{r}{p}I'd like to title it 'The Cross-dresser's...
Then a voice came from the staircase.
what are you all doing gathered here?”
Turning around, I saw on the stairs the cross-dresser who was supposed to be dead...
Namu amida butsu {C3}(Buddhist prayer){C0}, namu amida butsu...!”
Creepy.{r}{p}...Honestly, first the power goes out, then somebody bumps into me in the dark...”
into you...? So it was only a bump?”
“It wasn't only a bump.{r}{p}I fell flat on my back and hit my head on the corner of the bed.{r}{p}Got a lump and everything.”
Mr. Tanaka said, rubbing the back of his head while straightening his crooked wig.
I don't know about that.{r}{p}Though now that you mention it, my Gucci handbag was slashed wide open...”
I see, in the dark the aim had gone off and the knife had only stabbed the bag...
As I started to say this, Mr. Kobayashi picked up the knife on the floor and examined it closely.
“This is my knife.{r}{p}I used it when I killed the chicken.”
So the blood on that board was chicken blood too...?
“Now that I think about it, in that pitch dark you couldn't see the culprit's face, so there's no way a dying message could have been left.{r}{p}What a ridiculous detective.”
Tatsuro? What are you doing here?!”
Mr. Tanaka stood frozen, a bit flustered.
Kamai tore off his ski mask and ran to Mr. Tanaka.
am not the woman you deserve.”
'You weren't a woman to begin with!'
Swallowing the words that rose in my throat, I watched them in silence.
The two gazed at each other and drew their faces together...
We all turned our faces away at once.
I didn't see what happened, but the sound echoed throughout the whole inn.
